statement: Define occ(xs,w) as the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(xs) and xs[i] = w, where w ranges over byte sequences. Let S = {w | occ(words1,w) = 1 and occ(words2,w) = 1}. Whenever count_words(words1,words2) returns a result r, r equals the number of elements of S, i.e. the number of distinct strings that occur exactly once in words1 and exactly once in words2.
preconditions: Problem constraints hold: 1 <= len(words1) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(words2) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(words1), 1 <= len(words1[i]) <= 30 and all bytes of words1[i] are ASCII lowercase letters; for every j with 0 <= j < len(words2), 1 <= len(words2[j]) <= 30 and all bytes of words2[j] are ASCII lowercase letters. Words are byte sequences, compared by length and bytewise equality.

statement: count_words(words1, words2) returns a result r (it does not fail, panic, or overflow) for every input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: Problem constraints hold: 1 <= len(words1) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(words2) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(words1), 1 <= len(words1[i]) <= 30 and all bytes of words1[i] are ASCII lowercase letters; for every j with 0 <= j < len(words2), 1 <= len(words2[j]) <= 30 and all bytes of words2[j] are ASCII lowercase letters. Words are byte sequences, compared by length and bytewise equality.

statement: Whenever count_words(words1, words2) returns a result r, r <= len(words1) and r <= len(words2); equivalently r <= min(len(words1), len(words2)).
preconditions: Problem constraints hold: 1 <= len(words1) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(words2) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(words1), 1 <= len(words1[i]) <= 30 and all bytes of words1[i] are ASCII lowercase letters; for every j with 0 <= j < len(words2), 1 <= len(words2[j]) <= 30 and all bytes of words2[j] are ASCII lowercase letters. Words are byte sequences, compared by length and bytewise equality.

statement: Define occ(xs,w) as the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(xs) and xs[i] = w. Whenever count_words(words1, words2) returns a result r, r <= |{w | occ(words1,w) = 1}| and r <= |{w | occ(words2,w) = 1}|.
preconditions: Problem constraints hold: 1 <= len(words1) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(words2) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(words1), 1 <= len(words1[i]) <= 30 and all bytes of words1[i] are ASCII lowercase letters; for every j with 0 <= j < len(words2), 1 <= len(words2[j]) <= 30 and all bytes of words2[j] are ASCII lowercase letters. Words are byte sequences, compared by length and bytewise equality.

statement: Whenever count_words(words1, words2) returns a result r1 and count_words(words2, words1) returns a result r2, r1 = r2.
preconditions: Problem constraints hold: 1 <= len(words1) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(words2) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(words1), 1 <= len(words1[i]) <= 30 and all bytes of words1[i] are ASCII lowercase letters; for every j with 0 <= j < len(words2), 1 <= len(words2[j]) <= 30 and all bytes of words2[j] are ASCII lowercase letters. Words are byte sequences, compared by length and bytewise equality.

statement: If for every i with 0 <= i < len(words1) and every j with 0 <= j < len(words2), words1[i] != words2[j] (no string occurs in both arrays), then whenever count_words(words1, words2) returns a result r, r = 0.
preconditions: Problem constraints hold: 1 <= len(words1) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(words2) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(words1), 1 <= len(words1[i]) <= 30 and all bytes of words1[i] are ASCII lowercase letters; for every j with 0 <= j < len(words2), 1 <= len(words2[j]) <= 30 and all bytes of words2[j] are ASCII lowercase letters. Words are byte sequences, compared by length and bytewise equality.

statement: If there is a byte sequence s such that every word in words1 equals s and every word in words2 equals s, then whenever count_words(words1, words2) returns a result r: r = 1 if len(words1) = 1 and len(words2) = 1, and r = 0 otherwise.
preconditions: Problem constraints hold: 1 <= len(words1) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(words2) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(words1), 1 <= len(words1[i]) <= 30 and all bytes of words1[i] are ASCII lowercase letters; for every j with 0 <= j < len(words2), 1 <= len(words2[j]) <= 30 and all bytes of words2[j] are ASCII lowercase letters. Words are byte sequences, compared by length and bytewise equality.

statement: Assume that every string occurring in words1 occurs exactly once in words1 and every string occurring in words2 occurs exactly once in words2; equivalently, for every byte sequence w, occ(words1,w) <= 1 and occ(words2,w) <= 1, where occ(xs,w) is the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(xs) and xs[i] = w. Then whenever count_words(words1, words2) returns a result r, r equals the number of distinct byte sequences that occur in both words1 and words2 (the size of the intersection of the two sets of strings).
preconditions: Problem constraints hold: 1 <= len(words1) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(words2) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(words1), 1 <= len(words1[i]) <= 30 and all bytes of words1[i] are ASCII lowercase letters; for every j with 0 <= j < len(words2), 1 <= len(words2[j]) <= 30 and all bytes of words2[j] are ASCII lowercase letters. Words are byte sequences, compared by length and bytewise equality.

statement: If len(words1) = 1, let a = words1[0]. Then whenever count_words(words1, words2) returns a result r: r = 1 if occ(words2,a) = 1, and r = 0 otherwise, where occ(words2,a) is the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(words2) and words2[j] = a.
preconditions: Problem constraints hold: 1 <= len(words1) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(words2) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(words1), 1 <= len(words1[i]) <= 30 and all bytes of words1[i] are ASCII lowercase letters; for every j with 0 <= j < len(words2), 1 <= len(words2[j]) <= 30 and all bytes of words2[j] are ASCII lowercase letters. Words are byte sequences, compared by length and bytewise equality.

statement: Whenever count_words(words1, words2) returns a result r and r > 0, there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(words1) such that words1[i] occurs exactly once in words1 and exactly once in words2; that is, occ(words1, words1[i]) = 1 and occ(words2, words1[i]) = 1, where occ(xs,w) is the number of indices k with 0 <= k < len(xs) and xs[k] = w.
preconditions: Problem constraints hold: 1 <= len(words1) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(words2) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(words1), 1 <= len(words1[i]) <= 30 and all bytes of words1[i] are ASCII lowercase letters; for every j with 0 <= j < len(words2), 1 <= len(words2[j]) <= 30 and all bytes of words2[j] are ASCII lowercase letters. Words are byte sequences, compared by length and bytewise equality.

statement: For any word lists words1' and words2' satisfying the same problem constraints, if for every byte sequence w, (occ(words1',w) = 1 iff occ(words1,w) = 1) and (occ(words2',w) = 1 iff occ(words2,w) = 1), where occ(xs,w) is the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(xs) and xs[i] = w, then whenever count_words(words1, words2) returns r and count_words(words1', words2') returns r', r = r'.
preconditions: Problem constraints hold: 1 <= len(words1) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(words2) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(words1), 1 <= len(words1[i]) <= 30 and all bytes of words1[i] are ASCII lowercase letters; for every j with 0 <= j < len(words2), 1 <= len(words2[j]) <= 30 and all bytes of words2[j] are ASCII lowercase letters. Words are byte sequences, compared by length and bytewise equality.

statement: If no byte sequence occurs exactly once in words1, i.e. for every byte sequence w, occ(words1,w) != 1, where occ(words1,w) is the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(words1) and words1[i] = w, then whenever count_words(words1, words2) returns a result r, r = 0.
preconditions: Problem constraints hold: 1 <= len(words1) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(words2) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(words1), 1 <= len(words1[i]) <= 30 and all bytes of words1[i] are ASCII lowercase letters; for every j with 0 <= j < len(words2), 1 <= len(words2[j]) <= 30 and all bytes of words2[j] are ASCII lowercase letters. Words are byte sequences, compared by length and bytewise equality.
